beats.text: An application begins by identifying what one small piece contributes. Between the curves y equals x and y equals x squared on the unit interval, each vertical strip has height upper curve minus lower curve.

Integrate that strip height over its width. The antiderivative is x squared over two minus x cubed over three, so the enclosed area is one sixth. Subtracting the curves first creates a new nonnegative height function.

Rotate the region under y equals x, from zero to two, around the horizontal axis. Each thin slice is a disk with radius x, so its area is pi x squared. Integrating slice area produces volume in cubic units.

The same accumulation logic computes mass from a varying linear density. A rod with density one plus x contributes density times a tiny length. Integrating from zero to two gives mass four, with units determined by the density.

practice.prompt: Find the area between y=2x and y=x² on 0≤x≤2. Show which curve is above the other.
Rotate the region under y=√x on 0≤x≤4 about the x-axis. Write the disk integral and compute the volume.
practice.answer: Disk radius is √x, so area is πx. V=∫₀⁴πx dx=8π cubic units.

practice.prompt: A 2 m rod has density 3x+1 kg/m at position x meters from one end. Find its mass and explain the units.
practice.answer: M=∫₀²(3x+1)dx=[3x²/2+x]₀²=8 kg. Density in kg/m multiplied by dx in meters gives kilograms.

takeaway: Identify the quantity contributed by one small slice before integrating: height, cross-sectional area, or density.
scope: Area between curves, disk volume, and mass from a nonuniform density.
title: Applications of integration
objective: Build area, volume, work, and average-value integrals with correct bounds and units.
